stories.headline: Bank of Korea delivers hawkish hold, new governor signals second-half rate hikes
stories.summary: At new Governor Shin Hyun-song's first Monetary Policy Board meeting on May 28, the Bank of Korea held its benchmark rate at 2.50% for a seventh straight meeting but delivered one of its most explicitly hawkish signals in years: two board members dissented in favor of an immediate hike, the dot plot showed a median of 3.00% within six months, and the 2026 growth forecast was revised up to 2.6%. Governor Shin cited inflation, exchange-rate weakness, and housing risks as reasons a rate hike is necessary 'at an appropriate time,' prompting analysts to forecast July and October increases.

stories.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix semiconductor boom drives trillion-dollar valuations, wage disputes, and policy debates
stories.summary: SK Hynix joined Samsung Electronics in the exclusive $1 trillion market-cap club this week, driven by explosive AI-chip demand; Samsung also began shipping industry-first HBM4E memory samples to global clients and surpassed Micron to take the top spot in automotive memory. The boom sparked subsidiary wage disputes (Samsung workers receiving bonuses of up to $400,000), political debate over sharing tech wealth, a sovereign wealth fund plan for semiconductor tax windfalls, and fresh concerns about inflation and housing pressure feeding back into the BOK's hawkish turn.

stories.headline: South Korea announces plan to develop domestically built nuclear-powered attack submarines by mid-2030s
stories.summary: On May 26, the Ministry of National Defense published a 31-page 'Basic Plan for the Development of the Republic of Korea Nuclear-Powered Submarine' — the Chang Bogo N Project — committing to build the country's first nuclear-powered attack boat entirely domestically, with the first vessel operational by the mid-2030s. Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back unveiled the plan at a Future Defense Strategy Committee meeting, citing the need to counter North Korea's submarine-launched nuclear threats. President Lee separately urged acceleration of the program alongside an early transfer of wartime operational control; U.S. Secretary of Defense Hegseth called the Opcon push a 'breath of fresh air.' Bilateral nuclear fuel negotiations were scheduled for June 2.

stories.headline: June 3 local elections dominate final-week campaigning amid accusations of election interference
stories.summary: With South Korea's ninth nationwide local elections set for June 3, the final week saw intense campaigning across battleground regions, with the DPK anchoring its message on President Lee's high approval ratings and the PPP framing the vote as a check on executive power. President Lee's Busan visit for Ocean Day — where he invoked late conservative President Kim Young-sam — was seized on by the PPP as improper electioneering; DPK leader Jeong Cheong-rae fired back at former President Park Geun-hye for PPP campaign appearances. Early voting opened May 30–31 and set a record 23.51% turnout.

stories.headline: PPP files criminal complaint against President Lee over exposed ballot during early voting
stories.summary: The People Power Party filed a complaint with police on May 30, alleging President Lee violated the Public Official Election Act by briefly stepping out of a voting booth and showing his ballot to an election official. PPP leader Jang Dong-hyeok called the exposure deliberate illegal campaigning and grounds for impeachment; a civic group filed a separate complaint against election commission officials for negligence. The DPK dismissed the allegations as a political stretch.

stories.headline: Lee administration marks first-year anniversary with assessment series and planned news conference
stories.summary: As President Lee Jae-myung approaches the first anniversary of his inauguration, the Korea Times published a multi-part retrospective examining his AI policy push, regional tourism strategy, and diplomatic navigation of US-China tensions and tariff headwinds. The Seoul Economic Daily noted GDP growth of 3.6% in Q1 2026 and KOSPI above 7,000 as headline economic achievements. Lee's office confirmed a 100-minute news conference, open to approximately 160 journalists, scheduled for the following month to lay out his second-year agenda.

stories.headline: Fatal Seosomun Overpass collapse prompts Lee to order sweeping safety accountability investigation
stories.summary: President Lee ordered a full investigation on May 28 after a demolition accident at the aging Seosomun Overpass in Seoul killed three workers, linking the incident to a concurrent rebar defect discovered at Samseong Station on the GTX-A transit line. Lee vowed to hold those responsible accountable 'regardless of rank or position' and tied the moment to the 10th anniversary of the Guui Station fatality, calling the incidents evidence that the public sector's 'money over safety' culture persists.

stories.headline: Court acquits former President Yoon of perjury in Han Duck-soo insurrection-related trial
stories.summary: A Seoul Central District Court ruled on May 28 that former President Yoon Suk-yeol, currently jailed on insurrection charges stemming from the December 2024 martial law declaration, could not be convicted of perjury for testimony he gave during former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's aiding-the-insurrection trial. The court found insufficient evidence that Yoon's statements about cabinet meeting procedures were deliberately false, noting a 'high possibility' he had pre-existing plans regardless of Han's recommendations. Yoon remains detained on the underlying insurrection charge.

stories.headline: South Korea and Japan discuss military logistics deal at Shangri-La Dialogue as defense minister holds bilateral talks
stories.summary: Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back attended the 23rd Asia Security Summit (Shangri-La Dialogue) in Singapore from May 29–31, holding bilateral talks with Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi. Seoul confirmed the two sides discussed the possibility of a military logistics support agreement, though South Korea remains cautious given historical sensitivities. A bilateral visit by Koizumi to Korea is under discussion for after the dialogue.

stories.headline: Starbucks Korea boss issues second apology over Gwangju massacre-linked ad campaign as Lee government draws criticism for public condemnation before facts were established
stories.summary: Starbucks Korea's operator, Shinsegae's Chung Yong-jin, issued a second apology over a marketing campaign widely perceived as mocking victims of the 1980 Gwangju pro-democracy massacre. President Lee publicly criticized the company on social media before the investigation was complete, which drew a JoongAng Daily op-ed accusing the administration of 'Newspeak' and using presidential authority to silence corporate actors.

stories.headline: Hanwha Group acquires 7.22% stake in Korea Aerospace Industries in rapid buying spree
stories.summary: Hanwha Group purchased approximately 340 billion won worth of Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) shares over 11 trading days, lifting its stake from below 5% to 7.22% and making it KAI's third-largest shareholder behind the Export-Import Bank of Korea and the National Pension Service. The move is seen as deepening Hanwha's position in South Korea's defense industrial base alongside KAI's KF-21 fighter program.

stories.headline: Lee warns against hotel price gouging ahead of BTS Busan concerts
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung publicly criticized Busan businesses that had sharply raised accommodation prices ahead of BTS's 'Arirang' World Tour concerts in the city, warning that price gouging could damage Busan's reputation and called for publishing a list of offending establishments. The statement was made during Lee's Busan visit on May 27.

stories.headline: Credit loans surge to five-year high as investors borrow to buy stocks in KOSPI rally
stories.summary: Outstanding credit loans at South Korea's five major banks surged in May at the fastest pace since April 2021 as retail investors took out loans to buy stocks amid a record-breaking KOSPI rally above 8,000. Separately, the National Pension Service cut its domestic bond ratio as BOK Governor Shin's hawkish signals pushed government-bond yields higher, intensifying tension in fixed-income markets.
